newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't to offer less coffee in next auction.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't to offer less coffee in next auction.

text.p: Brazil's government, disappointed at the low level of sales in its latest monthly coffee auction, will offer a smaller quantity to the market in its next sale, said a top commodity official.

"We sold less coffee than we expected. Because of this, there will a little less coffee in the next auction," said Mauricio Assis, head of the primary commodities department at the Industry and Commerce Ministry.
Some 326,188 60-kg bags were offered in the last auction on April 2, of which only 128,660 or 39.44 percent were sold.
Of the 300,273 bags open to exporters, the domestic roasting and the soluble industry, sales totaled only 102,745 bags.
The remaining 25,915 bags were made available only to the soluble industry, all of which were sold.
The size of the auction had been the largest so far in the 1996/97 year (July/June). In March the government had offered 256,990 bags and seen a near sell-out.
Domestic roasters have said that the low sales last week were due to overly high opening prices and problems in obtaining credit lines from Banco do Brasil.

This was against a background of sufficient market supply as demonstrated by an industry index which dropped to 3.91 points between March 31 and April 4, indicating continued good supply and its lowest level for the past three months.

Assis confirmed he would be meeting members of the private sector in April 11 but said the meeting was to have preliminary talks ahead of the next full session of Brazil's new coffee council, the CDPC, scheduled for May 5 in Minas Gerais state.
He also said he was likely to meet exporters next week as part of a regular series of get-togethers to discuss the progress of exports.

However, he said he thought it would be too early to begin discussions on any Brazilian proposals on market stabilisation plans from July 1997 amongst members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC).
The ACPC secretariat has asked members to send any suggestions to London by April 15. ((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
